summary: The 2026-09-13 closed-loop sessions ARE analysable with the existing tools: 8 of the 10 folders (155559, 160850, 161350, 161733, 163921, 165748, 170213, 173702) carry plans.jsonl (raw/action_raw 16x5/obs_rows_t/anchor_pose_used/ckpt_sha1) + policy_obs/{index.csv, meta.json with builder.grid.P1, obs/, depth/} + mpc_*.meta.json hardware.datum_tag_frame, so rov_gui/tools/policy_yaw_vs_can.py runs unchanged when given the folder path; 172416 and 172850 are SQUARE missions with no policy data. All policy plans were flown with A = data/20260910/0910_095252_train_umi_depth_5d_depth5d_9926_A_vitclip (vit_base_patch16_clip_224.openai) ep195 `model` weights, sha1 1e4655c2..., except the first 5 plans of 155559 (0907 resnet ckpt 794bb0ee, excluded). Result (A only, cam_bear depth-blob, z<=1.5 m, |bear|<=45 deg, L/R at |bear|>8 deg): pooled n=609, L/R 296/68, sign-agree 58 %, r +0.116, slope +0.015 deg/deg (GT +0.45), mean dyaw +0.01 deg; L-side mean dyaw -0.24 deg (53 % negative), R-side +1.74 deg (78 % positive); bin -90..-15: -0.06 deg vs GT -14.8. Three runs are L/R-balanced (163921 86L/35R, 170213 44L/6R, 173702 18L/25R) and pooled over them r +0.034, slope +0.004, sign 45 % -> with the NEW can, A is essentially non-responsive to can bearing (weak rightward bias only); this is the baseline a DINOv3 run must beat. Deploy/replay path: through the exact rov_gui.perception.dp_policy import path in rovgui-pose (torch 2.11.0+cu128, timm 1.0.29) a TransformerObsEncoder with model_name vit_large_patch16_dinov3 builds and forwards on CUDA: output (1,410,768) = 2x201 image tokens + 8 low-dim tokens, Linear(1024->768) projection, 303.9M encoder params, denoiser cond_pos_emb (1,411,768) (A: 403); huge_plus also builds (841.5M, 1280->768). So dp_policy_offline.py and policy_session_replay.py (both DpPolicySession) need no code change to accept a DINOv3-trained checkpoint, but such a checkpoint does not exist yet and the A denoiser weights are not reusable (token count differs). Caveat for replay on these sessions: policy_session_replay.mission_of() and policy_yaw_vs_can.Run take only the FIRST mpc_*.csv, while the 0913 sessions have 3-29 CSVs / 3-15 mission clocks each, so replay proprio (and map_bear) are only valid for first-mission plans; cam_bear (what is reported) needs no datum.

claims.claim: The 0913 closed-loop sessions are directly consumable by rov_gui/tools/policy_yaw_vs_can.py without code changes: run_folder() accepts a directory path (policy_yaw_vs_can.py:62-65), Run() needs mpc_*.meta.json hardware.datum_tag_frame (141-147), policy_obs/meta.json builder.grid.P1 (148-151; measured P1 fx 343.148, cx 328.589, cy 191.341) and policy_obs/index.csv t_capture+depth_png (154-158), and plans() needs raw+action_raw+obs_rows_t (164-173) — all present in 8 of 10 folders (0913_155559 70 installed plans/148 frames, 160850 129/290, 161350 25/56, 161733 759/1654 with 729 frame matches within 1 ms, 163921 1067/2560, 165748 42/91, 170213 183/440, 173702 491/1328; depth PNG 400x640 uint16 mm). 0913_172416 and 0913_172850 have no plans.jsonl/policy_obs (events.log: SQUARE missions under mpc_tuned/pid) and cannot be analysed. Every policy plan carries ckpt_sha1 1e4655c21faa... = data/20260910/0910_095252_train_umi_depth_5d_depth5d_9926_A_vitclip/checkpoints/epoch=0195 (.hydra/config.yaml:26 model_name vit_base_patch16_clip_224.openai = variant A, weights `model`, controller.json /policy/worker/session/ckpt_sha1_head) except the first 5 plans of 155559 (sha 794bb0ee = 2026.09.07 resnet34 selected.ckpt, events.log 15:56:00), which were excluded from the A pool.
claims.why_it_matters_here: Establishes that the encoder question is testable on existing data with the project's own metric, and pins exactly which checkpoint (A = ViT-CLIP ep195 `model`) produced every plan so the baseline is attributable.

claims.claim: Measured with the tool's own detector and defaults (cam_bear from depth blob, z<=1.5 m, |bear|<=45 deg, sign-agreement at |bear|>8 deg, knot-15 dyaw = action_raw[15,3]), A on the NEW can per run [run: near-range plans, L/C/R counts, sign-agree, r, slope deg/deg, mean dyaw; L-side mean/agree, R-side mean/agree]: 155559: 38, 37/1/0, 97 %, -0.48, -0.278, -2.66 (L -2.5/97 %, no R); 160850: 11, 9/0/2, 45 %, -0.29, -0.034, +0.11; 161350: 10, 10/0/0, 10 %, +0.62, +0.872, +1.51 (L +1.5/10 %); 161733: 91, 81/10/0, 75 %, +0.03, +0.004, -0.44 (L -0.5/75 %); 163921: 204, 86/83/35, 45 %, +0.05, +0.006, +0.59 (L +0.6/31 %, R +2.0/77 %); 165748: 13, 11/2/0, 91 %, -0.27, -0.111, -2.33; 170213: 74, 44/24/6, 32 %, -0.04, -0.007, +0.08 (L -0.1/25 %, R +2.8/83 %); 173702: 168, 18/125/25, 63 %, +0.05, +0.007, +0.20 (L +1.0/39 %, R +1.4/80 %). Pooled (609 plans, L/R 296/68): sign 58 %, r +0.116, slope +0.015 (GT +0.45), mean dyaw +0.01 deg; L side mean -0.24 deg (53 % negative), R side +1.74 deg (78 % positive); bins -90..-15: -0.06 deg vs GT -14.8, -15..-5: -1.87 vs -5.4, +5..+15: +1.39 vs +1.4, +15..+90: +1.12 vs +13.2. Only 163921, 170213, 173702 are L/R-balanced (>=5 each side); pooled over them (446 plans, L/R 148/66): sign 45 %, r +0.034, slope +0.004. Reading: A is essentially non-responsive to the new can (r ~ 0; a ~1.5-2.8 deg rightward nudge when the can is right, nothing when it is left); the high sign-agree in 155559/165748 is a constant -2.5 deg left turn on all-left runs, the trap the tool's docstring warns about. For comparison the 0908 old-can baseline was A 89 %/r +0.71 on the one balanced run 173106 (21L/15R) and 57 %/+0.15 pooled over 5 runs.
claims.why_it_matters_here: This is the concrete baseline a DINOv3 encoder run must beat on the same data and metric: pooled r +0.12 / slope +0.015 (balanced-run r +0.03) versus the training-label slope +0.45; it also shows the 0908 'A follows the can' result did not carry over to the new can in closed loop.

claims.claim: The deploy/replay loader accepts a DINOv3 ViT checkpoint without code changes, verified empirically in rovgui-pose (torch 2.11.0+cu128, timm 1.0.29) through the exact import path dp_policy uses (rov_gui.perception.dp_policy._import_upstream -> upstream diffusion_policy/model/vision/transformer_obs_encoder.TransformerObsEncoder, built with pretrained=False and the ckpt cfg's model_name, dp_policy.py:672-682): with the A checkpoint's shape_meta and model_name swapped to vit_large_patch16_dinov3 the encoder builds (transformer_obs_encoder.py:91-96 timm.create_model; 139-146 'vit' branch, feature_aggregation None = all tokens; 191-200 auto Linear(1024->768) projection because feature_size != n_emb 768), output_shape (1, 410, 768) = 2 frames x 201 tokens + 8 low-dim tokens (A: (1, 402, 768)), 303.9M encoder params, CUDA forward OK (250 ms cold, 1.25 GB peak); the denoiser then builds with max_cond_tokens 411 (cond_pos_emb (1,411,768) vs A's (1,403,768)). vit_huge_plus_patch16_dinov3 also builds (841.5M, Linear(1280->768), 3.52 GB peak). Both rov_gui/tools/dp_policy_offline.py (line 735) and rov_gui/tools/policy_session_replay.py (lines 203-207) instantiate dp_policy.DpPolicySession, so a DINOv3-trained checkpoint saved by the same DiffusionTransformerTimmPolicy workspace (checks at dp_policy.py:625-634 _target_ + DDIM, 651-654 transforms[0] RandomCrop, 711-712 strict load) would replay through the same path. Not testable end-to-end: no DINOv3-trained checkpoint exists, and the A checkpoint's denoiser weights cannot be reused (cond token count 403 vs 411), so a DINOv3 policy must be trained from scratch (denoiser included).

claims.why_it_matters_here: Answers whether the encoder question is testable offline with existing tooling: yes on the deploy side, the only missing piece is a trained DINOv3 checkpoint (training env is the blocker, not the replay path).

claims.claim: Replaying the 0913 sessions with another checkpoint (policy_session_replay.py --ckpt) is only valid for FIRST-mission plans as the tools stand: the 0913 folders are multi-engagement (155559: 4 mpc CSVs / 3 distinct mission clocks obs_t_mono-obs_t_rel; 161733: 3/3; 163921: 29/15; 173702: 9/9; plan obs_t_rel spans 0..330 s), but policy_session_replay.mission_of() returns the first mpc_*.csv only (lines 86-92) and MissionState reconstructs the low-dim proprio by np.interp on that CSV's t_traj (97-148, 237-243), so plans from later engagements get clamped/wrong proprio (images stay exact: obs_png lookup by obs_rows_t, 172-184). Likewise policy_yaw_vs_can.Run takes the datum from the first CSV (141-147), which invalidates map_bear/ray-intersection for these sessions; only cam_bear (datum-free) was reported above. plot_policy_map.py already iterates per mission (docstring, lines 85-98) so plotting is fine. A per-plan CSV selection keyed on the mission clock (or the record's `epoch`) would be needed to replay a DINOv3 checkpoint on all 2,761 A plans; alternatively --verify on the first missions quantifies the reconstruction error before trusting any cross-ckpt replay.

claims.why_it_matters_here: Defines what a like-for-like DINOv3-vs-A comparison on the 0913 observations can and cannot use without touching code: the yaw-vs-can metric is valid now, the cross-checkpoint replay needs a small per-mission fix or must be restricted to first missions.

gaps: No DINOv3-trained checkpoint exists, so the strict state-dict load (dp_policy.py:711-712) and a real replay were not exercised; only encoder/denoiser construction and a CUDA forward were verified in rovgui-pose.

The can detector is a heuristic depth blob (RANSAC floor + nearest compact blob); 0913_163921's ray-intersection residual (13.2 cm RMS) suggests the can moved or was misdetected in that run, and the closed-loop setting adds a selection effect (a responsive policy would drive |bearing| toward 0, thinning the |bear|>8 deg sample). No independent can-position ground truth (obj_px empty, no tag-anchored can note) was found for the 0913 sessions.

Balanced-run count is small and the right side is thin (66 R plans across the three balanced runs); the pooled r +0.116 is dominated by 0913_163921 and 173702 and has no noise floor here (no __replay_verify variant was produced for 0913).

The training-side blocker (umi2 timm 0.9.7 has no dinov3; pretrained weights are license-gated on the hub) was out of scope and not re-checked; a DINOv3 policy also cannot reuse A's denoiser (cond tokens 403 vs 411), so it is a from-scratch 200-epoch run before any of the above comparisons can be made.

The scratch JSON summary written by my script (yaw_vs_can_0913_lr.json) lives only in the session scratchpad; nothing was written into the repo (no journal/memory update), per the read-only instruction.
